Background Recent data have shown that γδ T cells can act as mediators for immune defense against tumors. Our previous study has demonstrated that persisting clonally expanded TRDV4 T cells might be relatively beneficial for the outcome of patients with T cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). However, little is known about the distribution and clonality of the TRDV repertoire in T cell receptor (TCR) of γδ T cells and their effects on the clinical outcome of patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The aim of this study was to assess whether the oligoclonal expansion of TCR V δ T cells could be used as an immune biomarker for AML outcome. Findings γδ T cells were sorted from the peripheral blood of 30 patients with untreated AML and 12 healthy donors. The complementarity-determining region 3 (CDR3) sizes of eight TCR V δ subfamily genes ( TRDV1 to TRDV8 ) were analyzed in sorted γδ T cells using RT-PCR and GeneScan. The most frequently expressed TRDV subfamilies in the AML patients were TRDV8 (86.67 %) and TRDV 2 (83.33 %), and the frequencies for TRDV1 , TRDV3 , TRDV4 , and TRDV6 were significantly lower than those in healthy individuals. The most frequent clonally expanded TRDV subfamilies in the AML patients included TRDV8 (56.67 %) and TRDV4 (40 %). The clonal expansion frequencies of the TRDV2 and TRDV4 T cells were significantly higher than those in healthy individuals, whereas a significantly lower TRDV1 clonal expansion frequency was observed in those with AML. Moreover, the oligoclones of TRDV4 and TRDV8 were independent protective factors for complete remission. Furthermore, the oligoclonal expansion frequencies of TRDV5 and TRDV6 in patients with relapse were significantly higher than those in non-recurrent cases. Conclusions To the best of our knowledge, we characterized for the first time a significant alteration in the distribution and clonality of the TRDV subfamily members in γδ T cells sorted from AML patients. Clonally expanded TRDV4 and TRDV8 T cells might contribute to the immune response directed against AML, while oligoclonal TRDV5 and TRDV6 might occur in patients who undergo relapse. While the function of such γδ T cell clones requires further investigation, TRDV γδ T cell clones might be potential immune biomarkers for AML outcome. molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.activity_type_context: Immune response in Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) and its clinical outcome (complete remission, relapse), encompassing AML pathogenesis and progression and overall leukemia immune response.
molecular_mechanism_and_relationship.mechanism_description: γδ T cells act as mediators for immune defense against tumors. Altered distribution and clonality of TRDV subfamilies in AML patients influence clinical outcomes. Specifically, clonally expanded TRDV4 and TRDV8 T cells might contribute to an anti-leukemia immune response and are suggested as reactive T cell clones. In contrast, oligoclonal TRDV5 and TRDV6 might occur in patients undergoing relapse, potentially indicating minimal residual disease. The specific molecular mechanisms underlying these changes in AML are noted to require further elucidation.
related_biomarkers: Percentage of blast cells in PB

dose_intensity_and_specificity.dose_comparison_summary: The study focuses on the differential expression and clonal expansion frequencies of TRDV subfamilies. Frequencies of expressed TRDV subfamilies are significantly lower in untreated AML patients compared to healthy individuals. Oligoclonal expansion frequencies of TRDV5 and TRDV6 are significantly higher in AML patients experiencing relapse compared to non-recurrent cases. A higher frequency of clonally expanded TRDV8 was also observed in MDS patients who developed AML.
dose_intensity_and_specificity.specificity_finding: Specific TRDV subfamilies demonstrate distinct roles in AML outcomes. Oligoclonal expansion of TRDV4 and TRDV8 are independent protective factors for complete remission, while oligoclonal expansion of TRDV5 and TRDV6 are independent risk factors for AML recurrence. The alteration in TRDV repertoire distribution in AML appears distinct from other hematological malignancies (e.g., MDS), suggesting that different γδ T cell subfamilies may be preferentially active depending on the disease and immune status. γδ T cells generally possess antitumor cytotoxicity, a value also seen in other hematological malignancies like MDS, MM, and CML.

clinical_implication_and_population.health_implication: Oligoclonal expansion of TRDV4 and TRDV8 T cells may offer a protective benefit for achieving complete remission in AML and represent an anti-leukemia immune status. Conversely, oligoclonal expansion of TRDV5 and TRDV6 T cells may indicate an adverse risk for relapse and could serve as indicators of minimal residual disease. A high percentage of blast cells in peripheral blood is also identified as a risk factor for complete remission. These TRDV γδ T cell clones are potential immune biomarkers for AML outcome, providing insights for leukemia immunotherapy.
clinical_implication_and_population.risk_classification: Protective benefit for complete remission (oligoclonal TRDV4, TRDV8 expansion); Adverse risk for complete remission (high blast cell percentage in PB); Adverse risk for AML recurrence (oligoclonal TRDV5, TRDV6 expansion); Diagnostic utility for AML outcome and antileukemia immune status (oligoclonal TCR V delta T cells).

biomarker_reliability_and_future_focus.reliability_assessment: The identification of TRDV4, TRDV8, TRDV5, and TRDV6 subfamilies as independent protective or risk factors for AML outcomes was supported by multivariate non-conditional logistic regression and multivariate stepwise regression analysis, suggesting statistical robustness. However, the study acknowledges that the function of these γδ T cell clones requires further investigation, especially in vitro and in vivo models (e.g., co-culture and mouse xenograft models). Confirmation of TRDV5 and TRDV6 as minimal residual disease indicators with a larger cohort is also needed. Overall, γδ T cell-based immunotherapy for AML is considered to be in its early stages, necessitating further elucidation of the immune characteristics of γδ T cells in AML.
recommended_alternatives: Further functional characterization of TCR V delta T cell subfamilies in co-culture models and mouse xenograft models.
